text:
Priya: handing over primary to @Luca for the 18:00->02:00 UTC window. Active latency pager for hosted text-gen (p99 ~ 1.8s -> 6s across some routes). main points: customer-impact on a small subset of PLG tenants, intermittent 500s for long context requests. attaching quick checklist and runbook links below. :handshake:

incidents-bot: Pager: HOSTED-TEXTGEN-LATENCY (sev-2) — triggered 30m ago. Affected routes: /v1/generate (model: redwood-7b-v2). Active incidents: 1. Assigned: Priya (primary).

Luca: taking. thanks priya. quick Q — any warm nodes or kv-cache pressure noted?

Priya: logs showed elevated evictions on KV cache (~30% eviction rate last 15m). No recent deploys. Autoscaler did one small upscale + burst but CPU saturated on a few pods.

Jordan: flagging potential coverage gap: if we lose a whole az, do we have immediate fallback to low-cost model variant? we might need to enable canary fallback policy if latency spikes further.

Maya: checklist for whoever is primary now (short version):
- Verify customer impact (support tag + list): `SELECT tenant_id FROM telemetry.alerts WHERE route='/v1/generate' AND status='error' LIMIT 50;`
- Check pod health: `kubectl get pods -n inference -l app=textgen -o wide`
- Check kv cache metrics: Dashboard -> Infra / KV Cache -> evictions/sec and hit-rate (last 1h)
- Force-invalidate problematic prefix cache: `curl -X POST "https://ops-api.internal/cache/invalidate" -d '{"prefix":"/tenants/<id>/ctx"}'` (only do for high-eviction tenants)
- Re-route heavy requests to 'redwood-7b-quant' variant for affected tenant(s): Console -> Routes -> Apply fallback to variant `redwood-7b-quant` (policy: immediate, ttl 15m)
- If pod CPU > 80% for >5m, trigger manual scale: `kubectl scale deployment/textgen --replicas=<current+2> -n inference`

Priya: quick commands I ran: 
```
# pod snapshot
kubectl top pods -n inference | sort -k3 -nr | head -n 8
# check logs for 500s
kubectl logs -n inference deployment/textgen --since=20m | grep "HTTP 500" | head -n 100
```
Result: two pods spiking 95% CPU, one returning repeated 500s with OOM warnings in model-worker logs (likely KV cache mem pressure).

Luca: I'll take pod-scale and fallback routing. @Jordan you hold secondary?

Jordan: yep I'll be secondary. quick ask: does support need a customer-impact blurb to patch into existing tickets?

Ella: support blurb (short): "We're investigating elevated latencies and intermittent 500s on text generation for a subset of tenants. Workaround: routing to a lower-memory variant has been enabled while we stabilize. ETA for full resolution TBD; we will update every 30 minutes." Use tag: `#incidents-hosted-textgen` and paste metrics snapshot.

Maya: runbook links (shortcuts):
- KV cache stall: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-cache-stall (steps: identify tenant prefixes, selective invalidation, mem cache resize)
- Pod OOM / high CPU: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pod-hotloop (steps: inspect stack traces, dump /proc, scale or restart)
- Fallback routing & canary: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/fallback-routing (console quick steps + api snippet)
- Escalation matrix: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/escalation (who to page for infra / model infra / infra-sre)

Priya: quick triage decision we made before handoff: 1) selective cache invalidation for top 3 tenants driving evictions, 2) manual scale + cordon unhealthy pod to force new provisioning, 3) enable fallback to `redwood-7b-quant` for 15m rolling. That reduced 500s but p99 still elevated.

Luca: actioning now: running `kubectl scale deployment/textgen --replicas=8 -n inference` and applying fallback via API:
```
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/routes/fallback -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","from_model":"redwood-7b-v2","to_model":"redwood-7b-quant","ttl":900}'
```
Status: scale command accepted; fallback API returned 202.

incidents-bot: Update logged: HOSTED-TEXTGEN-LATENCY — fallback policy applied, scale requested.

Jordan: monitoring. p50 looks fine, p95 improved ~30%, p99 still ~3.2s. Should we open a dedicated dedicated-capacity ticket for the larger tenants? maybe they'll need reserved capacity.

Priya: opened internal ticket INF-4321 for dedicated capacity eval and cc'd growth/sales for impacted PLG tenants. Link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/INF-4321

Maya: quick remediation hints if things worsen (cribsheet):
- If KV cache evictions > 50%: start rolling restart of textgen pods one at a time: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/textgen -n inference --field-selector=spec.nodeName=<node>`
- If errors switch from 500->429: likely throttling — check rate-limit logs and consider increasing quota for affected tenants temporarily via Console -> Quotas.
- If model-worker OOM persists after scale: switch to quantized variant or reduce `max_input_length` via feature flag for high-volume requests (feature flag path: Console -> Flags -> textgen.max_input_length).

Luca: note for handoff: @Luca primary -> @Jordan secondary at 02:00 UTC. If pager flares again at night, follow same quick checklist. If we see repeated OOMs after scale, page infra-sre oncall (see escalation runbook).

Priya: leaving a short summary for next primary: actions taken: selective cache invalidation (top 3 tenants), manual scale to 8 replicas, applied fallback to redwood-7b-quant for /v1/generate (ttl 15m), opened INF-4321 for capacity. Current status: degraded p99 but steady, support blurb posted.

Jordan: ack. copying steps into our shared handoff doc -> https://redwood.internal/handoffs/18-02-UTC (added runbook links + commands).

Maya: small reminder: add `#impact:partial` and `#customers:limited` tags to incident for downstream analytics.

Priya: done. I'm switching status to `snooze` and handing to @Luca now. ping me if anything weird. :v:
